body:
Interestingly, indexing with `nan` works, if it's the only element.

See this example for which I added an extra column 'a' compared to the initial post (to make it easier to follow):

```
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({'a': [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]}, index=pd.Index([np.nan, 100.0, 200.0, 300, 100.0]))
>>>
>>> df
       a
NaN    1
100.0  2
200.0  3
300.0  4
100.0  5
```

Indexing with `np.nan` works as expected...
```
>>> df.loc[np.nan, 'a']
1
```

... just like like indexing with a number...

```
>>> df.loc[200.0, 'a']
3
```


... or multiple index elements...

```
>>> df.loc[[100, 200], 'a']
100.0    2
100.0    5
200.0    3
Name: a, dtype: int64
```

... but as soon as `np.nan` is part of to the index, a `KeyError` is raised:

```
>>> df.loc[[100, 200, np.nan], 'a']
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "env/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1067, in __getitem__
    return self._getitem_tuple(key)
  File "env/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1247, in _getitem_tuple
    return self._getitem_lowerdim(tup)
  File "env/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 991, in _getitem_lowerdim
    return getattr(section, self.name)[new_key]
  File "env/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1073, in __getitem__
    return self._getitem_axis(maybe_callable, axis=axis)
  File "env/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1301, in _getitem_axis
    return self._getitem_iterable(key, axis=axis)
  File "env/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1239, in _getitem_iterable
    keyarr, indexer = self._get_listlike_indexer(key, axis)
  File "env/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1432, in _get_listlike_indexer
    keyarr, indexer = ax._get_indexer_strict(key, axis_name)
  File "env/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexes/base.py", line 6070, in _get_indexer_strict
    self._raise_if_missing(keyarr, indexer, axis_name)
  File "env/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexes/base.py", line 6133, in _raise_if_missing
    raise KeyError(f"{not_found} not in index")
KeyError: '[nan] not in index'
```

As soon as `np.nan` is used in a list (or similar), the `KeyError` occurs (Note: `df.loc[np.nan, 'a']` works just fine).

```
>>> df.loc[[np.nan], 'a']
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "env/blendopt-py38/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1067, in __getitem__
    return self._getitem_tuple(key)
  File "env/blendopt-py38/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1247, in _getitem_tuple
    return self._getitem_lowerdim(tup)
  File "env/blendopt-py38/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 991, in _getitem_lowerdim
    return getattr(section, self.name)[new_key]
  File "env/blendopt-py38/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1073, in __getitem__
    return self._getitem_axis(maybe_callable, axis=axis)
  File "env/blendopt-py38/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1301, in _getitem_axis
    return self._getitem_iterable(key, axis=axis)
  File "env/blendopt-py38/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1239, in _getitem_iterable
    keyarr, indexer = self._get_listlike_indexer(key, axis)
  File "env/blendopt-py38/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1432, in _get_listlike_indexer
    keyarr, indexer = ax._get_indexer_strict(key, axis_name)
  File "env/blendopt-py38/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexes/base.py", line 6070, in _get_indexer_strict
    self._raise_if_missing(keyarr, indexer, axis_name)
  File "env/blendopt-py38/lib64/python3.8/site-packages/pandas/core/indexes/base.py", line 6130, in _raise_if_missing
    raise KeyError(f"None of [{key}] are in the [{axis_name}]")
KeyError: "None of [Float64Index([nan], dtype='float64')] are in the [index]"
```

This is also an issue in pandas 2.0.0rc1

```
>>> df.loc[[np.nan], 'a']
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "envs/pandas2/lib64/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1097, in __getitem__
    return self._getitem_tuple(key)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "envs/pandas2/lib64/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1280, in _getitem_tuple
    return self._getitem_lowerdim(tup)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "envs/pandas2/lib64/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1024, in _getitem_lowerdim
    return getattr(section, self.name)[new_key]
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^
  File "envs/pandas2/lib64/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1103, in __getitem__
    return self._getitem_axis(maybe_callable, axis=axis)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "envs/pandas2/lib64/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1332, in _getitem_axis
    return self._getitem_iterable(key, axis=axis)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "envs/pandas2/lib64/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1272, in _getitem_iterable
    keyarr, indexer = self._get_listlike_indexer(key, axis)
                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "envs/pandas2/lib64/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/indexing.py", line 1462, in _get_listlike_indexer
    keyarr, indexer = ax._get_indexer_strict(key, axis_name)
                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "envs/pandas2/lib64/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/indexes/base.py", line 5873, in _get_indexer_strict
    self._raise_if_missing(keyarr, indexer, axis_name)
  File "envs/pandas2/lib64/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/indexes/base.py", line 5932, in _raise_if_missing
    raise KeyError(f"None of [{key}] are in the [{axis_name}]")
KeyError: "None of [Index([nan], dtype='object')] are in the [index]"
```

It seems that "all" that's missing to resolve this is to remove the check

```
    self._raise_if_missing(keyarr, indexer, axis_name)
```

in `pandas/core/indexes/base.py`, line 6070, in `_get_indexer_strict`


```
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> import numpy as np
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({'a': [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]}, index=pd.Index([np.nan, 100.0, 200.0, 300, 100.0]))
>>> df.loc[[np.nan], 'a']
100.0   NaN
Name: a, dtype: float64
>>> 
>>> 
>>> df.loc[[np.nan, np.nan], 'a']
100.0   NaN
100.0   NaN
Name: a, dtype: float64
```

Can this be done in pandas 1.5.x?

In the interim, would someone be able to propose a workaround that does the same thing (`Index` and `MultiIndex`)?

My current workaround is to monkeypatch `Index`, but that may hide required exceptions (although in `base.py` I couldn't find another place where `_raise_if_missing` is called):

```
from pandas.core.indexes.base import Index

def _ignore_if_missing(self, *args, **kwargs):
    pass

setattr(Index, '_raise_if_missing', _ignore_if_missing)
```
@ssche I was able to reproduce this error. I am going to work on fixing this and submit a pull request as soon as possible.
